killedBy: hud.css is syntactically whole has a rule for every class the HUD writes, so no class is silently dead
why:
Renames the verdict line's rule so the class the TypeScript writes has none. This is the dead-CSS class hud.css.test.ts exists for, and it is not cosmetic here: a

with no rule takes the browser's default 16px block margin, which on a pane that lists one row per connected pad pushes the channel bars down by a line per pad. The sweep over every class the HUD writes is what catches it; a test that only checked the classes it happened to think of would not.
